title: Meditating on Scripture
definition: Meditating on Scripture is the prayerful dwelling of the mind and heart upon God's Word so that its truth is understood, treasured, remembered, and obeyed.
summary: Biblical meditation is not emptying the mind but filling the heart with God's truth and turning that truth over in prayer.
christFocus: The written Word bears witness to Christ, and meditation deepens trust in Him, dependence on grace, and obedience to His commands.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Meditating on Scripture teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to meditating on scripture by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
